scenario.title: 工作太多，怎麼拒絕新任務
scenario.context: 在職場說「不」是一門藝術：要讓對方知道你真的沒辦法，又不能讓人覺得你不合作。這個單元也處理一組經典易混動詞：remember / stop / try 後面接 to V 和 V-ing，意思會完全不同。

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.en: Hey Minz, could you design a quick flyer for our event next week?
lines.zh: 嘿 Minz，你可以幫我們下週的活動做一張簡單的傳單嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I'd love to help, but my plate is full right now. I'm finishing two packaging projects.
lines.zh: 我很想幫忙，但我現在手上滿了，正在趕兩個包裝案。

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.en: It's really small. It would only take an hour.
lines.zh: 真的很小，大概只要一小時。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I believe you, but I'm already stretched thin. If I say yes, something else will slip.
lines.zh: 我相信你，但我已經分身乏術了。如果答應，其他事就會出包。

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.en: Fair enough. Do you know anyone else who could do it?
lines.zh: 有道理。你知道還有誰可以做嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Try asking Kai. He's been looking for more projects. And remember to send him the brand guide.
lines.zh: 試試問 Kai，他一直在找更多案子。還有記得把品牌規範寄給他。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: I can't believe you said no. You never say no.
lines.zh: 真不敢相信你拒絕了，你從來不拒絕的。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I know. I remember saying yes to everything last year, and I burned out.
lines.zh: 我知道。我記得去年什麼都答應，結果燃燒殆盡。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: You definitely bit off more than you could chew.
lines.zh: 你那時候絕對是自不量力了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: So I stopped taking on extra work. I tried saying no nicely, and it actually worked.
lines.zh: 所以我不再接額外的工作了。我試著好好地說不，結果真的有用。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: I need to learn that. My boss asks me to do weekend work, and I never refuse.
lines.zh: 我需要學這個。我老闆叫我週末工作，我從來不拒絕。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Next time, just say "No can do" with a smile.

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Ha! Maybe I'll try a more polite version first.
lines.zh: 哈！我可能先試試比較禮貌的版本。

patterns.en: I'm at full capacity right now.
I can't take this on right now.
Could it wait until next week?
What should I deprioritize if I take this on?
patterns.zh: 如果我接了，哪件事可以先放下？
patterns.note: 把決定權丟回給主管的聰明問法

patterns.en: I don't want to do a rushed job.
I'm afraid I'll have to pass.
Let me check my workload and get back to you.
patterns.zh: 我看一下工作量再回覆你。

chinglish.right: I'd love to help, but I'm at full capacity this week.
chinglish.why: 直接說 no time 很硬。先表達意願，再給具體原因。

chinglish.wrong: I stopped to take extra work.
chinglish.why: stop + to V 是「停下來去做某事」，stop + V-ing 才是「不再做」。意思完全相反。
提醒未來要做的事用 remember to V；remember V-ing 是「記得（過去）做過」。

chinglish.wrong: I will try my best to do.
chinglish.right: I'll do my best. / I'll try.
chinglish.why: try my best to do 後面少了受詞，聽起來不完整。

grammar.title: remember / stop / try + to V vs V-ing
grammar.oneLiner: 有些動詞接 to V 和 V-ing 意思完全不同：to V 通常指向未來或目的，V-ing 通常指向過去或動作本身。
whenToUse: remember to V：記得要去做（未來）。Remember to send it.
remember V-ing：記得做過（過去）。I remember saying yes to everything.
forget to V：忘了去做。/ forget V-ing：忘記做過（通常用 I'll never forget…）。
stop V-ing：停止做某事。I stopped taking extra work.
stop to V：停下來（為了）去做另一件事。I stopped to buy coffee.
try to V：努力嘗試（可能很難）。I tried to finish, but I couldn't.
try V-ing：試試看某個方法。Try asking Kai.
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 第 14 單元學過動詞後面接 to V 或 V-ing 要背。這個單元更進一步：同一個動詞，後面接不同形式，意思就不同。中文「記得」「停止」「試」後面動詞不變，完全靠語境判斷，所以台灣人常把 stop to take（停下來去接）和 stop taking（不再接）搞混，意思剛好相反。

examples.correct: Please remember to lock the door.
examples.note: 提醒未來的事用 to V。

examples.correct: I remember meeting her at a conference.
I stopped drinking coffee after 3 p.m.
On the way home, I stopped to get coffee.
If the file won't open, try restarting your laptop.
I tried to call you, but you didn't pick up.

quiz.question: Don't forget ___ me the files tonight.
quiz.explanation: 提醒未來的事：forget to V。

quiz.question: I've stopped ___ work emails on weekends. It's much healthier.
I remember ___ (meet) him at a party years ago.
The printer isn't working. Try ___ it off and on again.
We stopped ___ lunch on the way to Tainan.
quiz.explanation: 停下來去吃午餐：stop to V。

slang.usage: 婉拒工作時的經典說法。也說 I have a lot on my plate.

risk.note: 職場上很得體的拒絕方式。

examples.en: I'd love to join the committee, but my plate is full.
examples.zh: 我很想加入委員會，但我手上的事已經滿了。

examples.en: You have a lot on your plate. Let me help.
examples.zh: 你手上事情好多，我來幫忙。

slang.meaning: 分身乏術、資源被拉得太開
slang.usage: 人或團隊同時處理太多事，快撐不住。

examples.en: Our team is stretched thin with three launches this month.
examples.zh: 這個月有三個上線案，我們團隊分身乏術。

examples.en: I'm stretched too thin to take on anything else.
examples.zh: 我已經分身乏術，沒辦法再接別的。

slang.term: bite off more than you can chew
slang.usage: 接下超過自己能力或時間能處理的事。

risk.note: 自嘲很常見；說別人時帶點批評。

examples.en: I bit off more than I could chew with five clients at once.
examples.zh: 同時接五個客戶，我真是自不量力。

examples.en: Don't bite off more than you can chew in your first month.
examples.zh: 第一個月別貪多嚼不爛。

slang.usage: 輕鬆幽默地拒絕。據說源自洋涇濱英語，和第 10 單元的 long time no see 類似。

risk.note: 語氣輕鬆直接，對主管或客戶說可能太隨便。

examples.en: A: Can you work Saturday? B: Sorry, no can do.
examples.zh: A：你週六可以上班嗎？ B：抱歉，辦不到。

examples.en: Finish it by tonight? No can do.

review.question: I wish I ___ yes to so many projects last year.
review.explanation: 複習第 70 單元：過去的遺憾。

review.question: The more I take on, ___ stressed I get.
review.explanation: 複習第 69 單元：the more… the more…

review.question: I noticed him ___ (look) exhausted in the meeting.
Our team doesn't have the ___ for another project.
review.explanation: 複習第 55 單元：bandwidth = 餘力。

review.question: If I ___ this project, I'll miss my other deadlines.
"I stopped to answer the phone" means:
options: I don't answer the phone anymore.
I paused what I was doing in order to answer the phone.
review.explanation: stop to V = 停下來去做。
